news.Title: Google reportedly cuts Broadcom-designed TPU plans, eyes more MediaTek chips
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Google has reduced its planned 2027 shipments of Broadcom-designed AI chips while preparing to increase shipments of a MediaTek-designed alternative, according to technology supply-chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

The reported changes suggest Google is adjusting the mix of its custom AI processors as it navigates supply-chain constraints and limited data-center power—not necessarily pulling back on its broader AI ambitions.

In a recent post, Kuo said his latest industry survey indicated that Google had cut planned 2027 shipments of its Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by approximately 1 million units. That represents roughly 20% of the series' previously expected shipment volume.

Those figures imply a reduction from approximately 5 million chips to 4 million, although both totals are estimates derived from Kuo's reported numbers.

Most of the cuts affect the higher-priced 8i Max, also known as Whalefish, according to Kuo. That concentration could make the potential revenue impact more significant than the unit reduction alone suggests. However, his post did not provide pricing, contract terms or an estimate of the financial effect on Broadcom.

TPUs, or Tensor Processing Units, are Google's custom processors for AI workloads.

Kuo also reported that Google plans to increase 2027 shipments of the MediaTek-designed TPU 8t series, though the details remain unsettled.

The post did not specify the size of that increase, leaving it unclear whether additional 8t shipments would fully offset the reduction in the 8i family.

For investors, the report is directionally unfavorable for expectations surrounding Broadcom's Google TPU business and potentially favorable for MediaTek's role in Google's chip plans. It does not, however, establish the eventual revenue impact for either company.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

Kuo linked the change to Google's prioritization of frontier model development—the work involved in building its most advanced AI models.

According to his post, Google has repeatedly emphasized in recent months that frontier development receives first call on available computing resources. He characterized the changing TPU shipment mix as an adjustment to that priority amid tight supply chains and data-center power constraints.

Story Continues

The distinction matters: a reduction in one chip family does not automatically mean Google expects less overall demand for AI computing. It could instead reflect a decision to allocate scarce manufacturing capacity, infrastructure and electricity differently.

Kuo's post did not provide enough technical or economic detail to establish exactly why Google would favor additional 8t shipments over the affected 8i models.

Kuo, an analyst at TF International Securities best known for his technology supply-chain research, based the report on an industry survey rather than an official Google announcement.

With the shipment changes concerning 2027, the outlook remains subject to revisions. The key questions are how much Google ultimately increases its MediaTek-designed chip orders, whether those gains offset the Broadcom-designed reductions, and what the final mix means for supplier revenue.

Broadcom shares were down 8.9% on the day amid broad-based selling across the semiconductor sector. Alongside that wider weakness, Kuo's report raised concerns about lower expected Google TPU volumes, particularly for higher-priced models, and a potential shift toward MediaTek-designed chips.

The decline should not be attributed solely to the reported shipment changes. Still, the report adds uncertainty around Broadcom's future Google-related revenue as investors reassess expectations for AI-chip suppliers.

For now, Kuo's findings point to a potential reshuffling within Google's AI-chip supply chain—not clear evidence of a retreat from AI investment.

news.Title: Apple's secret AI agent shows John Ternus is done sitting out the AI race
news.Content: Apple ( AAPL ) scrubbed a job listing by Friday that showed it building its own AI agent. By then, Meta ( META ) and Anthropic ( ANT ) stock had already slid on what the post revealed. The listing described "an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does," browsing the web, working across apps, and writing code, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported Thursday . Then it vanished. "Apple killed the job listing, which is typical when they reveal too much about future plans," Gurman posted on X . It's the clearest sign yet that Apple is done watching the AI boom from the bleachers. John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook as CEO on Sept. 1, has been pressing software chief Craig Federighi to move faster , Bloomberg reported this month. Apple is aiming for a launch as soon as late next year. Investors didn't wait. Anthropic stock fell nearly 5% in late trading Thursday after the report, below the low of its first session as a public company . Meta stock fell about 1%, while Apple shares rose Thursday evening. On Friday, Apple was holding up far better than Meta and the Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ). The worry sits on Apple's own App Store shelf. AI assistants from its rivals hold four of the marketplace's top six free apps, led by Meta's Muse agent at No. 2. "Over 10 million people activating in the span of 45 days. I mean, that's pretty incredible," AMD ( AMD ) CEO Lisa Su told Yahoo Finance about Muse. Apple has been easing in all year, picking Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Gemini to power the new Siri in January. "As far as agentic capabilities, we think these are promising tools for users," Ternus said on his first earnings call as CEO. Apple also controls the door. Its next Mac update will require users to click through 14 steps to let ChatGPT run their computer, up from four today, Bloomberg reported. Is Apple still behind in AI? Somebody still has to pay for the AI build-out. So far, it isn't Apple. Apple's capital spending , or capex — what a company spends on long-lasting assets like buildings and equipment — fell nearly 30% to about $9 billion in its latest fiscal year. Meanwhile, Microsoft ( MSFT ), Meta, Alphabet, and Amazon ( AMZN ) spent more than $600 billion over four quarters. Apple's research budget jumped about $11 billion, more than its entire capex bill. For the heavy lifting, it rents, paying Google about $1 billion a year for Gemini, according to Bloomberg. An agent could change that math. Agents grind through multistep tasks in the background, which takes far more computing than answering a question. CFO Kevan Parekh said Apple is "in very, very early stages of understanding the kind of mix of those costs." Story Continues That's a risk for Wall Street's favorite AI hedge . Apple is up nearly 30% this year, while Meta and Alphabet are down roughly 9% to 13%. Apple may not get to stay a spectator. Luke Kawa of Sherwood News told Yahoo Finance this month that "even if you're not interested in the AI boom, the AI boom is interested in you." news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Dropped Again Today
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock tumbled 14% through 11 a.m. ET Friday morning, the same day it was supposed to soar in reaction to a big 8-for-1 stock split . And why?

I don't know about you, but I blame TrendForce.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

TrendForce sounds the alarm on NAND

Let me not bury the headline: Sandisk stock cost $750 per share yesterday, and it costs only $81 per share today. That feels like a big drop, but most of it's because each of Sandisk's yesterday-shares just got chopped up into eight pieces. Had no split happened, Sandisk stock would probably cost closer to $650 per share today.

That's still a huge drop from $750. So aside from the stock split, what's going wrong with Sandisk?

That's where TrendForce comes in. As StreetInsider.com reports today, memory-market research firm TrendForce just published a negative forecast for NAND flash memory demand in 2027.

Major Chinese cloud providers are likely to cut orders for enterprise SSD memory next year, warns TrendForce, and those cuts will be larger in size than any offsetting increase in U.S. AI-driven demand. This decrease in demand may eliminate pricing pressure on NAND chips, forcing NAND prices to stay flat or even decline 5% sequentially in Q1 2027.

What this means for Sandisk

This news gets worse. Cuts are already showing up in the spot market, where NAND prices are already down 20% from previously. As Chinese companies keep cutting purchases, the NAND supply-demand imbalance may disappear, and NAND prices may keep on falling "from Q2 2027 onward."

Now, the good news is that Sandisk already has "roughly half of its fiscal 2027 NAND bit supply and approximately two-thirds of its fiscal 2028 supply" locked in under long-term contracts. The bad news is that, once those supply contracts end -- so too could profitable NAND prices for Sandisk .

news.Title: Investing in Women-Run Companies? 5 Stocks to Consider
news.Content:
An updated edition of the Sept. 24, 2026 article.

Women-run companies are increasingly gaining investors' attention as female executives take on key leadership roles and drive business growth across diverse industries. These leaders are bringing fresh perspectives to corporate strategies, emphasizing operational efficiency, disciplined capital allocation, innovation and long-term sustainability. Their ability to navigate market challenges, identify emerging opportunities and strengthen competitive positioning can create a solid foundation for sustained profitability. For investors seeking long-term growth and value creation, companies led by women with proven leadership capabilities, sound financial strategies and strong execution offer compelling investment opportunities.

The latest reports paint a nuanced picture: women are becoming a structural force in U.S. entrepreneurship, even as funding and systemic gaps persist. One of the clearest takeaways is scale. Women now own more than 40% of all U.S. businesses, employing roughly 12.6 million people and generating $2.8 trillion in revenues. Growth has also been faster than that of male-owned firms, with women-owned businesses expanding nearly twice as quickly between 2022 and 2025. This shift signals that female entrepreneurship is no longer niche—it is central to the U.S. small- and mid-sized business ecosystem, particularly in services, consumer, healthcare and increasingly tech-enabled sectors. The data suggests women are not just starting companies, but building durable, employment-generating enterprises, a key driver of long-term economic resilience.

Female founders are increasingly gaining traction in AI and next-generation technology markets, which have become the primary destinations for venture capital. This indicates a shift from traditional sectors into high-value, innovation-driven markets, positioning women at the center of future growth themes. According to PitchBook's 2025 Female Founders report, U.S. female-founded startups raised a record $73.6 billion in venture capital in 2025, representing 27.7% of total U.S. VC deal value, the highest share on record. Importantly, AI accounted for roughly two-thirds of all venture dollars invested in female-founded startups.

At the same time, capital is becoming more concentrated in fewer, larger deals—often in AI—suggesting that while top-tier female-led companies are scaling rapidly, broader participation remains uneven.

Despite meaningful progress, female founders continue to face significant challenges in accessing venture capital. Funding disparities remain pronounced, even as women-led businesses have demonstrated strong capital discipline, efficient use of resources and the ability to generate competitive investment outcomes.

Despite funding challenges, women-led companies continue to drive innovation and resilience, making them attractive investment opportunities. If you want to capitalize on it, our Women Run Companies Screen will help you spot high-potential stocks in this space.

Investors seeking to capitalize on growth opportunities across diverse industries may consider Hasbro, Inc. HAS, a leading player in the toys and entertainment industry; Arista Networks, Inc. ANET, a provider of cloud networking solutions; Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, a major player in the technology and digital advertising space; Booz Allen Hamilton Holding Corporation BAH, a provider of technology and management consulting services to government agencies; and The Walt Disney Company DIS, a global leader in media and entertainment. These companies are well-positioned to benefit from industry-specific growth opportunities, supported by their established market presence, strategic initiatives and focus on long-term value creation.

Story Continues

5 Women-Run Company Stocks to Keep an Eye On

Hasbro : Gina Goetter, chief financial officer (CFO) and chief operating officer (COO) of Hasbro, has played an important role in strengthening the company's financial discipline, improving operational efficiency and advancing its business transformation. Since joining Hasbro in May 2023, she has overseen financial planning, treasury, investor relations, supply chain operations and business analysis. Her leadership has supported Hasbro's efforts to simplify operations, optimize costs and improve profitability while directing investments toward high-growth opportunities in digital gaming and intellectual property licensing. Her combined financial and operational responsibilities have also helped align business decisions with long-term profitability and shareholder returns.

Goetter's focus on operational efficiency and cost management has been reflected in Hasbro's latest financial performance. In the third quarter of 2026, revenues increased 15% year over year to approximately $1.6 billion, while adjusted operating profit surged 52% to $541 million. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased 73% to $2.90. For the first nine months of 2026, adjusted operating profit rose 35% to $1.11 billion, with adjusted operating margin expanding 440 basis points (bps) to 29.7%. The company's cost transformation program generated $105 million in savings during the nine-month period, highlighting progress in improving productivity and controlling expenses. However, favorable product mix and tariff refunds also contributed to profitability.

Goetter has also been instrumental in shaping Hasbro's capital allocation strategy, balancing business investments, debt reduction and shareholder returns. During the first nine months of 2026, Hasbro returned $445 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases while deploying $226 million toward debt reduction and prefunding upcoming maturities. Supported by stronger operating performance, management raised its 2026 adjusted operating margin guidance to 27-28% and adjusted EBITDA expectations to $1.575-$1.625 billion. Her continued emphasis on cost efficiency, financial flexibility and disciplined capital allocation is expected to support Hasbro's profitability and long-term shareholder value creation. Currently, Hasbro sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Arista : Jayshree Ullal, chief executive officer (CEO) and chairperson of Arista, has played a pivotal role in transforming the company into a leading provider of cloud networking and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure solutions. Since joining Arista as its founding CEO in 2008, she has spearheaded its expansion across hyperscale cloud, enterprise networking and data center markets. Her strategic focus on innovation, software-driven networking and customer-centric solutions has strengthened Arista's competitive position. Under her leadership, the company has advanced its Arista 2.0 strategy, emphasizing AI networking, high-performance Ethernet switching and cloud-scale infrastructure to capitalize on growing demand from hyperscalers and enterprise customers.

Ullal's strategic vision has been reflected in Arista's strong financial performance. In the third quarter of 2026, revenues surged 58.5% year over year to a record $3.66 billion, marking the company's highest year-over-year revenue growth since its initial public offering. Non-GAAP EPS increased 55.8% to $1.20 from 77 cents in the year-ago period. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 50 bps to 49.1%, highlighting healthy profitability despite continued investments in innovation and business expansion. Strong demand for AI infrastructure, cloud networking and next-generation Ethernet solutions supported the company's growth momentum.

Ullal continues to drive Arista's long-term growth through investments in AI networking architectures, product innovation and expansion into adjacent markets. The company's development of advanced Ethernet solutions, AI-focused switching platforms and scalable networking technologies is expected to strengthen its position in the rapidly expanding AI infrastructure market. Reflecting this momentum, Arista expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenues of $3.9-$4 billion, with a non-GAAP operating margin of 48-49% and adjusted earnings of $1.26-$1.30 per share. Her emphasis on technological leadership, operational efficiency and strategic expansion is expected to support sustained revenue growth, profitability and long-term shareholder value creation, although customer concentration and supply-chain constraints remain key risks. Currently, Arista carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Alphabet : Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer (CIO) of Alphabet and Google, has played a significant role in strengthening the company's financial discipline, investment strategy and long-term growth prospects. Having served as CFO from 2015 to July 2024, she helped establish a disciplined approach to financial management and capital allocation. In her current role, Porat oversees corporate investments, venture capital initiatives through GV and CapitalG, the Other Bets portfolio, and real estate and infrastructure investments. Her leadership has been instrumental in aligning Alphabet's investment priorities with emerging opportunities in AI, cloud computing and next-generation technologies.

Porat's emphasis on strategic investments and financial discipline remains relevant to Alphabet's expanding operations. In the third quarter of 2026, Alphabet's revenues increased 25% year over year to $127.6 billion, supported by strong demand across Google Services and Google Cloud. Google Cloud revenues surged 103% to $30.7 billion, reflecting robust adoption of AI infrastructure and enterprise solutions. Consolidated operating income increased 30% to $40.6 billion, while operating margin stood at 31.8%. Although these results reflect broader management efforts rather than Porat's direct contribution alone, they highlight the scale of Alphabet's growth opportunities and the importance of disciplined investment decisions.

Porat continues to influence Alphabet's long-term strategy through investments in infrastructure, emerging businesses and innovative technologies. With the company maintaining its 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $195-$205 billion, disciplined capital allocation remains critical to supporting AI-driven expansion while managing rising infrastructure costs. Her oversight of strategic investments and the Other Bets portfolio, including emerging technology businesses, could help Alphabet diversify its revenue streams beyond advertising and cloud services. However, substantial investment requirements and uncertain returns from newer ventures remain key challenges. Porat's focus on financial flexibility, infrastructure development and long-term investment opportunities is expected to support Alphabet's competitive position and shareholder value creation. Currently, Alphabet carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Booz Allen : Kristine Martin Anderson, president and COO of Booz Allen, has played a significant role in strengthening the company's operational efficiency, business transformation and strategic growth initiatives. Since joining Booz Allen in 2006, she has held several leadership positions, including president of the Civil Sector, before becoming COO in June 2022 and assuming the additional role of president in May 2026. Her leadership has focused on improving operational performance, accelerating technology-driven transformation and aligning business operations with growing demand for advanced defense, intelligence and civilian government solutions. She has also supported the company's transition toward higher-value technology offerings, including AI, cybersecurity and digital modernization.

Anderson's focus on operational discipline and business execution remains important to Booz Allen's financial performance. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues declined 3.9% year over year to $2.78 billion, primarily reflecting slower procurement activity and delayed program starts, particularly among civilian government customers. However, adjusted earnings per share increased 18.1% to $1.76 from $1.49 in the year-ago quarter. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $313 million, with the adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 10 basis points to 11.3%. The company's total backlog increased 2% year over year to approximately $41 billion, reflecting continued demand for its technology solutions despite near-term revenue pressures.

Anderson continues to play an important role in advancing Booz Allen's operational transformation and strengthening its position in high-growth technology markets. Her emphasis on efficient resource utilization, improved program execution and business modernization is expected to support profitability and long-term growth. Reflecting improving business expectations, Booz Allen maintained its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $11.3-$11.6 billion while raising its adjusted earnings per share outlook to $6.50-$6.70. However, federal spending uncertainties and procurement delays remain challenges. Anderson's continued focus on operational efficiency, technology innovation and strategic execution could help Booz Allen navigate these pressures and support long-term shareholder value creation. Currently, Booz Allen carries a Zacks Rank #3.

Disney : Dana Walden, president and chief creative officer of Disney, has played a significant role in strengthening the company's entertainment portfolio, expanding its streaming business and driving content innovation. Since joining Disney in 2019, she has overseen major television and streaming operations, helping establish Disney+ and Hulu as key growth drivers. Her leadership contributed to the streaming businesses achieving profitability through improved content strategies, stronger audience engagement and international expansion. Following her appointment as president and chief creative officer in March 2026, Walden assumed broader responsibility for integrating Disney's film, television, streaming, gaming and digital entertainment operations, strengthening coordination across its creative businesses.

Walden's strategic contributions are reflected in Disney's improving entertainment and streaming performance. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Disney's total revenues increased 16% year over year to $25.95 billion, while adjusted EPS rose to $1.77 from $1.11. Entertainment segment operating income surged 92% to $1.33 billion from $691 million, supported by higher subscription revenues and stronger content sales. Subscription video-on-demand revenues increased 19% to $6.05 billion, reflecting subscriber growth and improved monetization. Although these results reflect broader company initiatives and benefited from an additional operating week, they highlight progress in businesses central to Walden's leadership responsibilities.

Walden continues to shape Disney's long-term growth strategy by bringing its creative businesses closer together and strengthening connections between storytelling, streaming platforms and digital entertainment. Her focus on premium content, franchise development and international expansion is expected to support subscriber engagement, advertising opportunities and revenue diversification. Disney's established brands, including Marvel, Pixar and Lucasfilm, provide opportunities to extend intellectual property across films, television and gaming. However, rising content production costs and intense streaming competition remain challenges. Walden's emphasis on creative innovation, operational coordination and audience engagement could strengthen Disney's competitive position and support sustainable profitability and long-term shareholder value creation. Currently, Disney carries a Zacks Rank #3.

news.Title: Tech Outages Spur Emergency Buying: Costco-Heavy ETFs in Focus
news.Content:
A series of tech outages and disruptions involving Apple AAPL, JPMorgan Chase JPM, Microsoft MSFT and U.S. airlines over the past week has rattled consumers. Worried that a cyberattack or another major system failure could disrupt everyday life, some shoppers have started stocking up on emergency supplies.

Walmart WMT has noticed a modest increase in demand for certain essentials. Walmart isn't the only retailer benefiting from the trend. Costco COST is also seeing increased demand for emergency-preparedness products, according to Mizuho, as reported by Yahoo Finance.

In the final week of October, Costco's U.S. comparable sales, excluding gasoline, increased 11% to 12%, according to Mizuho. The firm said this strong growth continued through the first two weeks of November.

Costco Sees a Rush for Emergency Supplies

In a client note, Mizuho analyst David Bellinger said consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the grounding of U.S. airline flights and alarming social media posts has fueled emergency-supply purchases at Costco, according to the above-mentioned Yahoo Finance report.

The demand has been particularly strong for generators. As of Nov. 15, 21 of the 26 high-priced generator models listed online were sold out, Bellinger noted.

He added that these one-time sales boosts, along with pantry stocking and Costco's value appeal heading into the holiday season, are supporting an already elevated valuation for the retailer's shares.

Should You Buy This One-Time Boost at Costco?

Investors should note that Costco trades at a rich valuation at current levels. The stock trades at forward price/earnings (P/E) of 48.24X, versus 20.40X for the Retail - Discount Stores industry. Costco shares trade at a price/book (P/B) ratio of 13.57X versus the industry average of 7.79X

Based on short-term price targets offered by 32 analysts, the average price target for Costco comes to $1,101.53. The forecasts range from a low of $781.00 to a high of $1,315.00. news.Title: Can Verizon's $4 Billion AI Contracts Add Meaningful Growth in 2027?
news.Content:
Verizon Communications Inc. VZ has signed approximately $4 billion of AI infrastructure contracts, with revenues expected to begin contributing in 2027. The agreements give the company a new way to monetize fiber connectivity and network locations beyond traditional wireless and broadband services.

The opportunity is relevant because Verizon's broader growth outlook remains modest. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for 2027 revenues of $142.71 billion, representing 1.8% growth from the 2026 estimate.

Verizon's AI Deals Create a New Revenue Avenue

Verizon announced an agreement valued at more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services in October 2026, adding to a previously announced Google dark fiber agreement worth more than $1 billion. Management said signed AI infrastructure contracts, including edge computing agreements, now total approximately $4 billion.

The counterparties also underscore the scale of AI infrastructure demand. Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN reported 39% year-over-year growth in AWS sales in the third quarter of 2026, while Alphabet Inc. GOOGL said AI infrastructure and solutions were major drivers of Google Cloud growth. Verizon's network assets give it a way to participate in that spending without changing its core connectivity model.

VZ's 2027 Timing Makes the Contracts Investable

Management expects revenues from the signed AI infrastructure agreements to begin contributing in 2027. That timing creates a defined period for investors to watch whether AI Connect starts adding to Verizon's existing mobility and broadband service revenue base.

The contracts are described as long-duration arrangements, which could support recurring infrastructure revenues as deployments progress. They also broaden Verizon's growth mix at a time when the Zacks Consensus Estimate points to only 1.8% sales growth in 2027.

Verizon Limits AI Spending Within Current Capex

Management expects attractive margins and modest, contract-linked incremental capital requirements from AI Connect. Verizon's unchanged 2026 capital expenditure outlook of $16-$16.5 billion already includes success-based AI Connect investment.

That matters because the company is simultaneously funding fiber expansion, spectrum and network modernization. Keeping near-term AI spending inside the existing capital framework reduces the risk that the new business immediately requires a separate step-up in planned expenditures.

VZ's Core Business Still Shapes the Upside

AI infrastructure remains an incremental opportunity rather than a substitute for Verizon's core operations. Third-quarter 2026 postpaid average service revenue per account declined 1.9% year over year to $168.08, showing that better subscriber trends have not eliminated monetization pressure.

Fixed wireless growth has also slowed. Third-quarter fixed wireless access additions fell 39.1% year over year to 159,000. AI Connect becomes more meaningful to the investment case if its revenue contribution adds growth alongside, rather than simply offsetting, pressure in traditional connectivity businesses.

Story Continues

Verizon's Style Scores Temper the AI Story

The signed contracts give Verizon a credible new infrastructure revenue avenue with customer commitments from major technology companies and contributions expected to begin in 2027. Their importance should rise if the business delivers incremental revenue while maintaining the modest capital requirements management expects.

VZ currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It also has a Value Score of A, Growth Score of C, Momentum Score of D and VGM Score of B. The favorable Value and VGM Scores support the stock's broader investment profile, while the midrange Growth Score and weaker Momentum Score indicate that the AI opportunity has not translated into a uniformly strong growth-and-momentum setup. The current combination supports a measured view as execution becomes more visible in 2027.

news.Title: Meta Platforms (META) Down 8.1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
news.Content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Meta Platforms (META). Shares have lost about 8.1% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Meta Platforms due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Meta Platforms, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

META's Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise Y/Y on Ad Growth

Meta Platforms reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share, which increased 2.1% year over year, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 13.50%. Revenues jumped 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, surpassing the consensus mark by 1.88%.

Strong advertising demand, AI-driven engagement and improving monetization supported revenue growth. Ad impressions increased 10% year over year, while the average price per ad advanced 14%. However, higher infrastructure spending and legal expenses pressured operating profitability.

META's Ad Business Fuels Revenue Growth

Family of Apps revenues, which accounted for 99.3% of total revenues, increased 26.4% year over year to $64.16 billion. Advertising revenues rose 25.9% to $63.06 billion, supported by healthy engagement, user growth and ad-load optimization across Meta's platforms.

Family of Apps other revenues surged 59% year over year to $1.1 billion, primarily driven by WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions.

Reality Labs revenues declined 5.7% to $443 million as lower Quest headset sales more than offset strong growth in AI glasses revenues.

Meta's AI Investments Boost User Engagement

Family daily active people averaged 3.64 billion in September, up 3% year over year. Average revenue per person increased to $17.72 from $14.46 in the year-ago quarter, reflecting improving monetization across the company's ecosystem.

Instagram global time spent per user reached an all-time high, growing at a double-digit rate. Facebook Reels engagement also achieved record levels, while Threads time spent per user increased more than 20%. AI-powered recommendation improvements lifted Instagram Reels viewing time by more than 4%.

Meta's advertising systems continued delivering measurable performance gains. The company's expanded GEM ranking model increased offsite campaign conversions by 1.7% and app advertising conversions by 9.6%. Nearly 10 million advertisers used generative AI creative tools during the reported quarter.

Story Continues

Meta's Muse Expansion Opens New Revenue Opportunities

Meta launched its Muse personal agent and Muse Wonder frontier AI model during the reported quarter. More than 10 million users in the United States and Canada adopted Muse within approximately six weeks, with about 25% using the service on a given day.

Shopping emerged as Muse's leading use case, accounting for more than a quarter of active users, with average purchases exceeding $200. Meta plans to monetize the platform through commerce fees, premium subscriptions and enterprise services.

The company expects Muse's computing efficiency to improve more than tenfold over the coming year. These improvements could support broader adoption while reducing the cost of serving individual users.

META's Rising Costs Weigh on Operating Margins

Total costs and expenses surged 68.1% year over year to $51.61 billion. The increase included a $9.89 billion charge related to the August 2026 agreement with U.S. state attorneys general concerning teen mental health litigation.

Operating income declined 36.8% year over year to $12.99 billion, while operating margin contracted to 20% from 40% reported in the year-ago quarter. Excluding the legal charge, operating income would have increased 11% year over year. Infrastructure investments, depreciation, cloud spending and third-party AI token costs remained major expense drivers.

Family of Apps operating income fell 31.4% year over year to $17.12 billion. Reality Labs operating loss narrowed to $4.13 billion from $4.43 billion, reflecting improving segment profitability despite continued investment.

META's Cash Flow Reflects Heavy AI Infrastructure Spending

Meta ended September with $82.45 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Total debt stood at approximately $83.66 billion.

Cash flow from operating activities totaled $32.79 billion, compared with $30 billion a year earlier. Capital expenditures, including finance lease principal payments, increased to $34.91 billion from $19.37 billion, resulting in negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion.

The company also announced plans to establish a new non-voting Class C common stock, with shareholders receiving one new share for each existing share. The distribution is expected to effectively result in a two-for-one stock split in January 2027.

Meta's Outlook Signals Sustained Growth and Investment

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Meta expects revenues between $73 billion and $76 billion. The guidance incorporates an approximately 1% foreign currency headwind to year-over-year growth.

The company raised its 2026 expense outlook to $175-$179 billion, incorporating the litigation charge. Capital expenditure guidance was narrowed to $135-$145 billion from $130-$145 billion.

Meta expects Reality Labs operating losses of $18-$19 billion in 2026, a decline compared with 2025. Reality Labs losses are expected to further narrow to roughly $15 billion in 2027.

The company anticipates strong revenue growth through 2027, supported by advertising improvements, AI advancements and emerging monetization opportunities.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

In the past month, investors have witnessed a upward trend in fresh estimates.

VGM Scores

Currently, Meta Platforms has a nice Growth Score of B, though it is lagging a lot on the Momentum Score front with a D. However, the stock has a grade of B on the value side, putting it in the second quintile for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of B. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Notably, Meta Platforms has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

news.Title: Why Is Lam Research (LRCX) Down 11.5% Since Last Earnings Report?
news.Content:
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for Lam Research (LRCX). Shares have lost about 11.5% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Lam Research due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Lam Research Corporation before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

Lam Research Q1 Earnings Beat on Systems Sales and Margin Gains

Lam Research reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $2.20 per share, up 74.6% year over year and 20.9% sequentially. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.17 by 1.38%, supported by favorable product mix and improving operating leverage.

Revenues jumped 54.4% from the prior-year quarter and 22.3% sequentially to $8.22 billion, beating the consensus mark of $8.14 billion by 0.98%. Growth reflected strong foundry and NAND investments, while customer support posted its fourth consecutive quarterly revenue record.

LRCX Systems Revenues Jump on NAND Conversions

Systems revenues rose 61.6% year over year and 34.9% sequentially to $5.73 billion. Memory made up 46% of systems revenues compared with 34% a year earlier, with its dollar contribution more than doubling.

Non-volatile memory accounted for 26% of systems revenues, up from 23% in the previous quarter. NAND sales increased about 40% sequentially, benefiting from conversions to 256-layer-and-above devices and initial investments in 384-layer technology. DRAM contributed 20%, versus 23% sequentially, as spending supported DDR5 and high-bandwidth memory.

Lam Research's Foundry Business Hits New High

Foundry reached record revenues, representing 46% of systems sales versus 44% in the June quarter. Demand came from leading-edge chipmaking and advanced packaging as well as mature-node capacity spending in China.

China represented 35% of total revenues, up from 26% in the previous quarter, with domestic and multinational customers contributing. Korea generated 20% of revenues, unchanged sequentially, while Taiwan accounted for 18%, down from 27%. Lam Research expects China's revenue share to fall significantly in the December quarter.

LRCX Support Revenues Reach Fourth Straight Record

Customer support-related revenues and other reached $2.49 billion, up 40% year over year and 0.6% sequentially. The Customer Support Business Group ("CSBG") benefited from high equipment utilization, NAND upgrades and demand for spares and services.

Story Continues

The company's Equipment Intelligence offerings and Dextro maintenance cobots helped win performance-based contracts with multiple memory manufacturers. Management expects CSBG revenue growth of more than 30% in calendar year 2026 and more than 15% in calendar year 2027.

Lam Research's Margins Rise Despite Higher Costs

Non-GAAP gross margin climbed 180 basis points year over year and 40 basis points sequentially to a record 52.4%, aided by favorable customer and product mix. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 40.2%, rising 520 basis points year over year and 180 basis points sequentially.

Non-GAAP operating expenses increased to $1 billion from $916 million in the previous quarter, primarily on higher incentive compensation tied to profitability. The company also stepped up investment in product programs, with research and development comprising roughly two-thirds of total operating expenses. Its non-GAAP tax rate increased to 16.5% from 11%, reflecting higher U.S. taxation of foreign earnings and shifts in the geographic income mix.

LRCX Sees AI Fueling Equipment Market's Growth

Lam Research expects calendar year 2026 wafer fabrication equipment spending in the mid-$150-billion range and projects more than $200 billion in 2027. DRAM is expected to lead growth, followed by leading-edge foundry and NAND. Management also projects calendar year 2026 systems revenue growth well above 40%.

In foundry and DRAM, its Akara etch and Aether dry resist products are gaining traction. Management lifted its cumulative Aether revenue outlook to approximately $2.5 billion by decade-end, up roughly $1 billion from its prior view. Panel plating systems have reached more than 20 customers, reflecting opportunities in advanced packaging.

Lam Research Generates Record Free Cash Flow

Operating cash flow increased to $3.50 billion from $1.46 billion in the June quarter, lifting free cash flow to a record $3.24 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash grew to $7.45 billion from $5.60 billion.

Inventory increased to $4.55 billion from $4.28 billion as Lam Research prepared for higher demand, but inventory turns improved to 3.4 from 3.0. Capital expenditures rose to $258 million from $189 million for laboratory and manufacturing expansion. The company repurchased about $1.01 billion in shares and paid $325 million in dividends.

LRCX Projects Higher December Earnings

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Lam Research expects revenues of $8.60 billion, plus or minus $400 million. Non-GAAP earnings are projected at $2.33 per share, plus or minus 15 cents, based on approximately 1.253 billion shares.

The company forecasts a non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, plus or minus one percentage point, and an operating margin of 40.5%, plus or minus one percentage point. Management noted that December revenue guidance would have been slightly higher without near-term supply constraints, while customer mix is expected to weigh on gross margin.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

In the past month, investors have witnessed a upward trend in estimates revision.

VGM Scores

Currently, Lam Research has a great Growth Score of A, though it is lagging a bit on the Momentum Score front with a B. However, the stock has a grade of D on the value side, putting it in the bottom 40% for value investors.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of B. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Notably, Lam Research has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

news.Title: What UBS Sees in Meta (META) Amid Heavy AI Spending
news.Content:
We just published a list of the 10 Potential Multibagger Stocks to Research for Long-Term Growth and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META ) ranked 7th on this list.

Reuters reported on November 5 that the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315, its deepest one-day drop in 19 months, while the S&P 500 lost 4.36% and about $3 trillion in market value disappeared. The trigger was Democratic wins in Congress, including in states where opposition to new data centers has grown. That stoked fears that tougher regulation could slow the AI buildout that helped lift stocks to records this year. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged more than 12% on the day, according to the same report, and for anyone searching for stocks that could double over three to five years, a selloff of that size moves the conversation from momentum to staying power.

Why AI Took the Biggest Hit

Melissa Brown, a global head of investment decision research, told Reuters that investors appear to be recognizing that new lawmakers and governors want to slow AI infrastructure development. She added that the AI growth story has largely depended on building out the supporting infrastructure, so any slowdown raises real concerns. Those concerns fall hardest on companies whose growth is tied to data center spending. Our ranking of AI infrastructure stocks to hold for the long term covers that group in more detail.

The weakness carried into the following week. Reuters reported on November 16 that the Nasdaq tumbled 2.5% and the S&P 500 dropped nearly 2%, as fallout from the resignation of a leading chipmaker's chief executive soured enthusiasm for AI stocks. Rate worries added to the pressure. According to the Associated Press, minutes released on November 18 showed that nearly all Federal Reserve officials expect a 25-basis-point rate increase in December, and two floated a 50-basis-point move.

What Long-Term Investors Weigh

Not everyone read the November 5 selloff as the start of a longer slide. Jed Ellerbroek, a portfolio manager, told Reuters it felt like the capitulation phase for companies that benefit from data center spending. Ipek Ozkardeskaya, a senior analyst, added that investors buying into a major AI public offering may sell existing tech holdings to pay for it. That concern showed up on November 19, when Reuters reported that the Nasdaq turned negative at midday as the AI developer's record-setting debut cast a cloud over AI-linked stocks. That leaves a market weighing policy risk, borrowing costs and AI demand all at once, and our list of undervalued growth stocks looks at the valuation side of that trade-off.

Story Continues

Meta made it to our list because it is one of the 10 stocks most popular among analysts and investors, with a market cap of $1.54 trillion. UBS resumed coverage of Meta Platforms with a Buy rating and an $815 price target on November 17. Meta runs Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp, along with Reality Labs, its virtual and augmented reality unit, and investors keep asking whether WhatsApp can become a meaningful business beyond advertising . In its third quarter of 2026, which ended September 30, 2026, revenue rose 26% to $64.60 billion, and nine-month revenue rose 29%. Operating income fell because of a $9.89 billion charge tied to an agreement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health litigation.

The bigger debate is cost. Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures of as much as $145 billion. Meta priced a $15 billion five-part bond sale on November 3 to help fund AI infrastructure, followed by €9 billion of euro bonds on November 4. Supporters note that the stock trades at 17.67 times forward earnings for a business growing revenue at a double-digit pace. Meta also plans to create nonvoting Class C shares in January 2027, paid as a one-for-one dividend that the company expects to act like a 2-for-1 split, and its release says the dividend does not change any shareholder's voting power.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of META as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. In its third quarter of 2026, which ended September 30, 2026, consolidated revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, and Google Cloud revenue reached $30.7 billion, up 103%.

Growth was not enough to settle investors. Capital expenditures of $51.4 billion exceeded operating cash flow and left free cash flow negative by $9.1 billion. Bulls see a cloud business that is doubling and a forward P/E of 18.56, though some ask whether that valuation accounts for Waymo's potential . Skeptics focus on the cash burn. Investors will also watch whether the AI ecosystem pitched at Ignite turns into paying demand beyond the $677 billion backlog, and whether security bundles can generate more profit per customer .

news.Title: Elon Musk sends stark signal to Tesla stock investors
news.Content: Elon Musk is not done taking the driver out of the car. Speaking at the DealBook Summit on Nov. 18, the Tesla CEO said the company plans an autonomous version of the Model Y "that would not have steering wheels or pedals and would be good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people," according to Benzinga . The new Model Y would sit alongside the Cybercab, Tesla's two-seat Robotaxi, which Musk has said could handle the majority of passenger miles. "We still need autonomous vehicles if you've got 4 or 6, or a whole family," he said, though he offered no further details or timeline. Musk made the remarks when asked whether Tesla's business would focus solely on autonomy going forward. His answer pointed to a lineup built around seating needs rather than driving. "It's going to make sense for us to make cars that can seat different amounts of people," he said. Elon Musk plans for new Model Y with no steering wheel Musk also had praise for the Model Y L, the six-seat version of the SUV, calling it Tesla's "most popular" model. "I think we should probably change all the Model Y production to the Y L because it's what most people seem to want," Musk said, according to Benzinga . Also read: Elon Musk gives SpaceX stock investors something new to consider The Model Y matters because it carries Tesla's business. Nearly all the vehicles Tesla delivered in the third quarter were Model 3 sedans and Model Y SUVs, with the Cybertruck and other models making up only a sliver of sales. It already does much of the work in Tesla's driverless fleet as well. Most of the Robotaxis Tesla has registered in Texas are Cybercab vehicles, while a smaller group of modified Model Y is on the road in Austin, with Dallas expected to follow. Tesla goes all in on the Cybercab Musk is putting serious money behind the two-seater. Tesla plans to spend about $3.3 billion expanding its factory near Berlin, with a new building designed to produce up to 1 million vehicles a year, Reuters confirmed . Construction is expected to start in the first half of 2027, and Cybercab production there is planned for 2029. The Cybertruck is making way at home. On Nov. 5, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory to free up space for the Cybercab, adding that the order backlog is "far more than we can make before dismantling the line," EV reported . Tesla shares rose about 5% the next day. The exit will take a little longer than first planned. Musk has since pushed the end of production to late summer 2027 to fill open orders, and buyers who do not get a truck will have their deposits returned. Story Continues The Cybertruck never came close to the sales Musk once promised, as its high price, unusual steel design, and a string of recalls weighed on demand. Some buyers can now get a Cybercab of their own. "Select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use," with deliveries expected to start in December, Tesla said, according to StockTwits . Owners must pay for Tesla's self-driving software, and the cars will operate only "in supported service areas." Owners could soon join the Robotaxi network Tesla's Robotaxi service has been spreading across Texas and beyond, with Austin as its first home. In April, it expanded to Dallas and Houston, where videos posted by Tesla showed Model Y SUVs running without a driver or a front-seat safety monitor. Musk now says private owners could get a piece of the action. "Coming soon," he wrote on X, replying to an Uber driver on Nov. 16. "If things [go] well, may start trials next month. Much better to manage a fleet of cars than have to drive just one car by yourself!" He did not name cities or explain how owners would be paid. For Tesla, owner cars could be a cheap way to grow. JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta called them "another capital-light source of supply," since Tesla would not have to buy those vehicles itself, TIKR noted. Tesla's own earlier timeline pointed to customer cars joining the fleet around the second quarter of next year. More Tesla: Tesla stock sellers should pump their brakes, 5-star analyst says Bank of America resets Tesla forecast as Robotaxi miles double Tesla wants to sell a car with no steering wheel this year Investors have heard similar promises before. Back in 2019, Musk said Robotaxis could hit the road the following year, according to CNBC , with owners keeping most of the fares. In July 2025, he said owner cars would join the network "confidently next year," Fortune noted . Electrek 's Fred Lambert summed up the gap bluntly: "Not one of them can run their car as a robotaxi." What it means for Tesla investors The autonomy push is now the core of the Tesla story. The Cybercab must prove it can run reliably, attract paying riders, and earn enough to cover what it costs to build. The Cybertruck exit shows how heavily Tesla is betting on that outcome, according to Reuters . Regulators remain a wild card. Tesla has not said whether it holds all the clearances needed for commercial Cybercab service, and its own filings warn that future growth depends in part on "customer acceptance of autonomous driving." Several federal agencies have also asked the company for information about its self-driving systems. Musk has previously said the Robotaxi network could combine elements of Uber and Airbnb. A steering-wheel-free Model Y for families would fill the gap the two-seat Cybercab leaves behind, but without a timeline, investors will have to take Musk at his word for now. Related: Elon Musk shares troubling outlook for America's debt This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 20, 2026, where it first appeared in the Automotive section. news.Title: Robinhood Markets vs. Nu: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As digital transformation continues to sweep through the global financial landscape, investors are comparing Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD) and Nu (NYSE:NU) to see which stock offers the best growth potential through 2027.

Robinhood disrupted the domestic brokerage industry by democratizing access to trading and cryptocurrency for millions of users. Nu is a dominant digital bank in Latin America, providing low-cost financial services to a massive, underserved population. Both companies represent a shift away from traditional banking toward mobile-first, technology-driven financial ecosystems.

The case for Robinhood Markets

Robinhood provides a multifaceted platform for retail investors, offering stocks, Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), and digital banking services. It recently expanded into institutional-grade services and introduced a credit card to deepen its relationship with users. According to its latest annual report, the company relies on partners like Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) for cloud infrastructure and Morningstar (NASDAQ:MORN) for research data.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $5.1 billion, an increase of roughly 21.1%. The company reported net income of approximately $2 billion during this time frame. This performance reflects a significant stabilization in its business model compared to previous years when trading volumes were more volatile.

As of Robinhood's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was about 1.3. This ratio measures how much debt a company uses relative to the value owned by shareholders. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $1.6 billion. Free cash flow is the cash left over after a company pays for its operations and capital expenditures.

The case for Nu

Nu operates as a digital-first bank, providing credit cards, personal loans, and savings accounts to millions of customers. It focuses on underbanked populations in Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, using lower overhead costs to offer better rates than traditional incumbents. The company's rapid expansion has made it one of the largest financial institutions in its region.

In the 12 months ended June 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $19.4 billion, an increase of approximately 53.2%. Net income for the period was roughly $3.6 billion. This growth highlights the scale of the digital banking shift occurring across emerging markets as users move away from physical branch locations.

As of Nu's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was about 0.5, and the current ratio was roughly 0.6. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $3.5 billion, providing capital to fund further international expansion.

Story Continues

Risk profile comparison

Robinhood Markets faces significant regulatory and legal uncertainty regarding its payment for order flow practices and the classification of its event contracts. These legal challenges, which include scrutiny from state gaming regulators, could impact its future revenue streams. Additionally, the company is highly dependent on third parties like Amazon for its underlying cloud technology infrastructure.

Nu faces risks associated with operating in emerging markets, where economic volatility and currency fluctuations can impact its reported results. The company must also manage credit risks as it expands its lending products to a broader customer base during different economic cycles. Since it operates as a bank, it is subject to rigorous capital requirements and oversight by various international financial regulators.

Valuation comparison

While Nu offers a significantly lower forward P/E multiple, Robinhood carries a higher premium that reflects its diverse expansion into different financial services and trading asset classes.

Metric

Robinhood Markets

Forward P/E

38.3

13.7

P/B ratio

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

The P/B ratio compares the stock price with the company's book value, which represents its assets minus its liabilities. Investors frequently use this metric to evaluate bank stocks. A lower P/B ratio indicates that a stock is less expensive relative to its paper value.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Neither of these stocks is something I'd normally invest in, because I'm a pretty conservative investor. Nu does not appeal to me given my past negative experiences with emerging market stocks (once bitten, twice shy). I don't find Robinhood attractive because at a previous publication I worked at, we rated brokerages. Robinhood was consistently low-scoring, and users were not shy about saying so. In particular, respondents reported that it has poor customer service. Contrast that with a competitor like Schwab (NYSE:SCHW), which has online chat (with real people), a phone line, and even physical branches. And while Robinhood may have pioneered commission-free trading, that's table stakes now.

Both of these companies went public in 2021. Let's see how their stocks have performed since:

HOOD data by YCharts

Nu does not compare favorably here; its stock hasn't even kept pace with inflation. Robinhood has delivered a strong performance, but it's seen a fair amount of volatility along the way. Of course, past performance is no indication of future results. But if I had to choose between these two, my vote would be for Robinhood.

news.Title: Can INTC Capitalize on AI Growth Through Its Expanded Microsoft Deal?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC is strengthening its position in the cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market with an expanded long-term partnership with Microsoft Corporation MSFT. The initiative reflects Intel's efforts to expand its data center business, advance semiconductor technologies and capitalize on growing demand for AI-driven cloud infrastructure.

Under the agreement, Intel and Microsoft will enhance Azure infrastructure by combining Intel's processors and advanced packaging technologies with Microsoft's cloud engineering expertise. Intel Foundry's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB) advanced packaging technology will be used by Microsoft for the first time in its first-party Azure silicon. The collaboration also confirms multi-year supply capacity for Intel Xeon processors, including next-generation server CPUs codenamed Diamond Rapids.

Intel will work with Microsoft on Xeon processors featuring Compute Express Link, QuickAssist Technology (QAT) and confidential computing to improve memory efficiency, database performance and cloud security. The company's Xeon 6 processors power Azure M-series v4 virtual machines, delivering up to 2.3 times better performance and memory flexibility. Intel QAT technology enables up to 2.5 times faster SQL backups, while its Trust Domain Extensions enhance security by protecting virtual machine memory and CPU register states.

The deal highlights Intel's focus on growing its data center and AI infrastructure business. Its long-term Xeon supply commitments, advanced packaging capabilities and deeper integration with Microsoft Azure could create additional growth opportunities as demand for scalable, high-performance and secure cloud computing continues to rise.

How Are Competitors Performing in the Cloud Market?

Intel faces competition from Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM and Advanced Micro Devices AMD. Qualcomm is expanding its presence in the cloud computing market through its Dragonfly AI200 platform, designed for large-scale AI inference workloads. The company partnered with Cirrascale Cloud Services to make the platform available for customer testing through its AI Innovation Cloud. Qualcomm has entered a multi-generation collaboration with Amazon to develop custom AI chips and advanced connectivity solutions for next-generation data centers.

AMD is advancing in the cloud infrastructure market through new server processor launches and collaborations with major cloud providers. Its 6th Gen EPYC processors are designed to handle demanding cloud, enterprise and AI workloads. AMD's 5th Gen EPYC processors are powering Google Cloud's TPU 8tx infrastructure, which supports confidential computing to protect sensitive AI models and data.

Story Continues

Shares of Intel have gained 65.8% over the past year against the industry's decline of 11%.

INTC's earnings estimates for 2026 have decreased 2% to $1.47 per share, while those for 2027 have declined 9.7% to $1.77 over the past 60 days.

news.Title: AMAT's AGS Gains From Growing Installed Base: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Applied Materials ' AMAT Applied Global Services ("AGS") is growing alongside fab utilization and the need to improve output, yield and ramp speed. AMAT's AGS business delivered a landmark performance in fiscal 2026, setting all-time revenue records and expanding profitability as chipmakers raced to add capacity and optimize yields for the AI era.

Backed by an expanding installed base and AI-driven service technologies, AGS enters fiscal 2027 poised to hit a major quarterly revenue milestone. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, AGS generated record revenues of $1,896 million, up 26% year over year on record services and spares, while lifting full-year revenues to $6,901 million.

AGS' non-GAAP operating margin reached 30.5%, up from 28.8% a year earlier. More than 37,000 chambers are connected to AMAT's AIx platform, a base growing over 20% annually. Management guides to about $2 billion in AGS revenues for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and expects second-quarter revenues near that level. Applied Materials targets at least 20% more service revenue per installed base tool by 2030.

Paired with high-resolution eBeam imaging and dedicated teams supporting more than 20 fab ramps and line expansions tracked for 2027, $AIx accelerates learning cycles and high-volume chip output while internal automation scales support functions efficiently. AGS is also tightly integrated into AMAT's co-innovation model via the EPIC Center in Silicon Valley, which brings together 15 announced partners to co-develop materials, equipment and processes.

How Competitors Fare Against AMAT

Since AMAT serves its own installed base through the AGS business, there are no competitors in this segment. But in the broader product category, AMAT competes with Lam Research LRCX and ASML Holding ASML.

ASML is experiencing strong demand from DRAM and logic customers, which are ramping leading-edge nodes using ASML's NXE:3800E EUV systems. Additionally, ASML noted that multiple DRAM customers are adopting EUV lithography, which helps shorten cycle time and lower costs. However, AMAT offers a broad range of WFE products that do not compete directly with ASML and Lam Research, making it a stock worth holding.

Lam Research secured multiple critical etch wins at a major DRAM manufacturer with its new Akara etch system, which supports 3D DRAM architectures. This was supported by LRCX's customer investments in DDR5, LPDDR5, and high-bandwidth memory. Additionally, Lam Research's Aether dry-resist technology was recently selected as the production tool of record for a leading DRAM customer, securing a foothold in this high-growth segment.

Story Continues

Applied Materials shares have climbed 31.9% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's appreciation of 2.2% and 0.3%, respectively.

news.Title: Amazon vs. Alibaba: Which E-Commerce Giant Has an Edge Right Now?
news.Content:
Amazon AMZN and Alibaba BABA are two of the world's largest e-commerce operators, each pairing a sprawling retail franchise with a fast-growing cloud business. Amazon leads online retail in the United States and beyond, while Alibaba anchors commerce in China through Taobao, Tmall and its quick commerce operations.

Both companies are now investing heavily in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, making AWS and Alibaba Cloud the key swing factors for long-term growth. Fresh results and outlooks make the comparison timely.

Let's delve deep and closely compare the fundamentals of the two stocks to determine which one is a better investment now.

The Case for AMZN Stock

Amazon's biggest strength is AWS, which is accelerating on AI demand. In the third quarter of 2026, AWS sales jumped 39% year over year to $46 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years, lifting the annualized revenue run rate to $184 billion. Management projects AWS revenue growth of more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028, backed by a $578 billion backlog. Amazon Bedrock has become the fastest-growing multibillion-dollar service in AWS history, with token volume rising nearly 17-fold. Custom chips Graviton and Trainium saved customers more than $2 billion in the quarter, and Amazon plans to make Trainium available outside AWS.

Retail is also becoming far more profitable. Amazon delivered a record operating margin of 13.9% in the quarter as operating income climbed to $28.1 billion, driven by lower cost to serve and higher-margin advertising. Newer bets, including Grocery, Pharmacy, Amazon Leo and Zoox, are progressing well, with Pharmacy users up 60% and Alexa for Shopping engagement up 570%.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Amazon expects net sales of $240-$247 billion, up 12-16% year over year, and operating income of $28.5-$33.5 billion versus $25 billion a year ago. Advertising revenues are expected to grow in the high teens.

Challenges remain. Amazon expects cash capital expenditure of about $220 billion in 2026, rising meaningfully in 2027, which pushed trailing 12-month free cash flow to an outflow of $42.4 billion. Amazon Leo's commercial launch also adds near-term costs. However, the robust backlog suggests these investments should generate solid returns.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMZN's 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.90 per share, indicating a 79.92% increase from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Amazon.com, Inc. Price and Consensus

Amazon.com, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Amazon.com, Inc. Quote

Story Continues

The Case for BABA Stock

Alibaba's strongest growth driver is AI cloud. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, AI Cloud and Compute Services revenues surged 53% year over year to RMB 61 billion ($9.09 billion), with external customer revenues up 64%. AI-related product revenues reached RMB 17.9 billion, marking the 13th straight quarter of triple-digit growth, while segment-adjusted EBITA jumped 121%. On Nov. 16, Alibaba launched Qwen4-Max, its most capable model to date, featuring 2.4 trillion parameters and a one-million-token context window.

E-commerce profitability is improving. Alibaba E-commerce Group's adjusted EBITA soared 243% to RMB 38.9 billion as quick commerce losses narrowed significantly, while quick commerce revenues grew 22%. Management expects these losses to keep narrowing in the December quarter, halve next year and turn profitable in instant retail by fiscal 2029.

However, the core business remains under pressure. China E-commerce revenues fell 5% year over year, and customer management revenues grew only 1% on a like-for-like basis amid cautious consumer spending and intense competition. International e-commerce revenues declined 8%.

More importantly, new U.S. compute export controls prompted management to lower its fiscal 2028 cloud revenue growth target to a 30-45% range, even as Alibaba ramps up its proprietary T-Head chips. Heavy spending also strains cash. Capital expenditure jumped 60% to RMB 50.5 billion, free cash flow was an outflow of RMB 34.5 billion, and the AI Labs and Applications segment posted an adjusted EBITA loss of RMB 10.5 billion. These factors make Alibaba's near-term trajectory less predictable despite its strong AI momentum.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 EPS is pegged at $6.49, reflecting a 0.9% upward revision over the past 30 days.

Alibaba Group Holding Limited Price and Consensus

Alibaba Group Holding Limited price-consensus-chart | Alibaba Group Holding Limited Quote

Valuation and Price Performance Comparison

Valuation-wise, Alibaba trades at a forward 12-month P/E of 10.52X, a steep discount to Amazon's 23.39X. Amazon's premium is justified by its visible AWS growth runway, $578 billion backlog and record profitability. Investors should closely track Amazon given its premium valuation and strong fundamentals, while holding Alibaba until regulatory clarity improves and a better entry point emerges.

AMZN vs. BABA P/E Ratio

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

On price performance, Amazon shares have gained 11.5% year to date, reflecting investor confidence in accelerating AWS growth and expanding margins. Alibaba shares have plunged 43.2% over the same time frame, weighed down by weak core e-commerce, export-control concerns and heavy cash burn.

AMZN Outperforms BABA YTD

Conclusion

Amazon holds a clear edge over Alibaba, backed by AWS' accelerating growth, a $578 billion backlog, a projected AWS growth rate above 40% in both 2027 and 2028, record operating margins and solid fourth-quarter guidance. Alibaba's AI cloud momentum and narrowing quick commerce losses are encouraging, but a shrinking core e-commerce business, export controls that have lowered its fiscal 2028 cloud growth target, and heavy cash burn cloud its outlook. Amazon's premium valuation is justified by superior visibility. Amazon holds better upside potential, and investors should track and hold AMZN stock while waiting for a better entry point for BABA. news.Title: Can CRWV Turn Its $132.5B Backlog Into Durable, Profitable AI Growth?
news.Content:
CoreWeave, Inc . CRWV ended the third quarter with $132.5 billion in revenue backlog, putting backlog conversion at the center of its investment case. The contracted demand gives the company substantial revenue visibility, but the eventual payoff depends on bringing infrastructure online while controlling capital intensity and financing costs.

That distinction matters because CoreWeave is already showing better operating leverage, yet net profitability remains constrained by interest expense. Investors therefore need to watch not only how quickly backlog grows, but how efficiently that backlog turns into revenues, cash flow and earnings.

CRWV's Backlog Sets Up a Major Revenue Conversion Test

Revenue backlog increased 138% year over year to $132.5 billion from $55.6 billion. The backlog chart on page 13 of CoreWeave's earnings presentation shows that 36% is expected to be recognized within 24 months, 38% within 25-48 months and the remaining 26% beyond 48 months.

Management also said more than half of the backlog is attached to contracts where customer delivery is expected to begin by the end of 2026. That creates a sizable near- and medium-term revenue opportunity, provided CoreWeave can deploy the required infrastructure on schedule.

CoreWeave's Capacity Build Must Match Contracted Demand

CoreWeave had more than 1.7 gigawatts of active power and more than 4.6 gigawatts of contracted power at Sept. 30, 2026. The company operated 52 active data centers and added more than 900 megawatts of contracted power during the third quarter, according to the infrastructure map and operating metrics on page 5 of its earnings presentation.

Management continues to expect more than 1.85 gigawatts of active power by year-end. It also said qualified demand is 10 times available capacity through 2027. The gap between contracted demand and active infrastructure means execution on power, data centers and equipment remains central to converting the backlog into recognized revenues.

CRWV's Pricing and Renewals Could Lift Asset Economics

CoreWeave raised pricing across cloud SKUs by about 25% in July and another 10% later in the third quarter. Pricing on prior-generation Ampere and Hopper GPUs increased 30-50% sequentially, indicating that older infrastructure can still command favorable economics in a capacity-constrained market.

Management said more than 130,000 GPUs will come off contract in 2027. At current pricing, those renewals could generate nearly $4 billion of incremental annualized revenues without additional capital spending. Another roughly 170,000 GPUs are scheduled to come off contract in 2028, potentially increasing the contribution from already-installed assets.

Those figures remain sensitive to future supply, demand and pricing. Renewal economics therefore represent potential operating leverage rather than guaranteed returns.

CoreWeave's Interest Burden Delays the Profit Payoff

Third-quarter net interest expense reached $846 million, up from $310 million a year earlier. Despite $207 million of GAAP operating income and $379 million of adjusted operating income, CoreWeave still reported a $709 million net loss.

Management expects fourth-quarter interest expense of $1.05-$1.15 billion. It projects adjusted net losses to decline meaningfully in 2027 and expects adjusted net income in the first half of 2028 and for full-year 2028.

The timing matters. Backlog can drive substantial revenue growth, but shareholder returns ultimately depend on operating cash flow and margins expanding faster than interest and infrastructure costs.

CRWV's Style Signals Temper the Backlog Opportunity

CoreWeave's $132.5 billion backlog gives the company unusually high visibility into future demand, while higher pricing, expanding capacity and potential GPU renewals provide paths to better asset economics. The risk is that the capital and financing required to fulfill those commitments absorb too much of the operating benefit.

news.Content:

Third-quarter results strengthened the growth case. Still, the stock's broader decline and weak momentum profile argue for caution on how durable the rebound may be.

CRWV's 14.5% Weekly Gain Meets a Mixed Trend

CoreWeave shares have fallen 48.3% over the past three months and 37.3% year to date. That backdrop makes the latest weekly advance notable, but it does not erase the damage from the broader selloff.

The stock's current forward 12-month price-to-sales multiple is 0.83X, below 3.53X for the Zacks sub-industry. The discount can attract investors after a sharp decline, though the company's losses and leverage help explain why valuation alone may not sustain the rebound.

CoreWeave's AI Demand Keeps the Growth Case Intact

CRWV's Backlog Offers Visibility but Demands Delivery

Revenue backlog reached $132.5 billion at the end of the third quarter, up 138% year over year. More than half is tied to contracts where customer delivery is expected to begin by the end of 2026, giving CoreWeave substantial multi-year revenue visibility.

That visibility still depends on execution. Active power exceeded 1.7 gigawatts at Sept. 30, 2026, and management maintained its target of more than 1.85 gigawatts by year-end, so converting backlog into revenues requires capacity to come online as planned.

CoreWeave's Debt Load Could Cap Further Upside

Capital expenditures were $14.5 billion in the quarter, and management now expects $37-$39 billion for 2026. Customer prepayments, delayed-draw term loans and operating cash flow support the funding plan, but the scale of required investment keeps financing risk central to the stock's outlook.
